'''Mary Newton Torrey''' (February 2, 1910 – January 7, 1998) was an American [[mathematical statistics|mathematical statistician]] and [[quality control]] specialist for [[Bell Laboratories]].{{r|contributors}}
With [[Harold F. Dodge]] at Bell Labs, she was an early contributor to the theory of [[acceptance sampling]].{{r|kt}}
The Dodge–Torrey continuous sampling plans are named after her and Dodge.{{r|sn|mr}}

Torrey was born in [[Worcester, Massachusetts]], and graduated in 1930 from [[Wellesley College]] as a Durant Scholar (Wellesley's highest honor) with a double major in mathematics and physics.{{r|contributors|wellesley}} In that year she joined the Quality Assurance Department of Bell Labs. While working there, she earned a master's degree in mathematical statistics from [[Columbia University]] in 1946.{{r|contributors}}

In 1958, she was elected to be a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] "for her contributions to the theory of sampling inspection, for her able analyses of engineering data, and for her clear and concise presentation of statistical quality control in electronics".{{r|fasa}} She was also a fellow of the [[American Society for Quality|American Society for Quality Control]].{{r|contributors}}

Torrey died on January 7, 1998, at the age of 87.<ref>[https://www.familytreenow.com/search/death/results?first=Mary&last=Torrey&dobyyyy=1910&rid=0s0&smck=ZWmYR9Fnn2LO8hNqRWfYsA Mary N Torrey]</ref><ref>[https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-10002-8131285/mary-n-torrey-in-us-social-security-death-index-ssdi Mary N Torrey]</ref>
